slides.title: Q3 2026 board update
slides.subtitle: Sample Co. is a fictional B2B software company. Every figure in this deck is sample data, invented for this example.
slides.author: CEO, Sample Co.

slides.title: Q3 beat plan, but SMB churn puts year-end ARR $230k short; we propose moving two hires to onboarding

points.headline: New business is healthy
points.detail: Q3 new ARR beat plan by 21%, the third straight quarter above plan.

points.headline: SMB churn now limits growth
points.detail: If the trend continues, year-end ARR lands about $230k below the $12.0M plan.

points.headline: The cause is SMB accounts that never finish setup
points.detail: Onboarding load per specialist rose 41% while the team stayed at two people.

points.headline: Move two Q4 sales hires to onboarding
points.detail: It saves $110k a year and recovers about $82k of Q4 ARR. We ask for two approvals today.

slides.notes: Lead with the ask; the rest of the deck is the proof.

slides.title: New ARR beat plan by 21% in Q3, the third straight quarter above plan
takeaways: Q3 new ARR was $1,150k against a $950k plan
Q1 and Q2 also beat plan, by $50k each
slides.source: metrics.csv (new ARR and plan new ARR by quarter). Beat = actual / plan - 1.

slides.title: Ending ARR of $11.05M beat plan by 1.4%, a smaller margin than new ARR because churn rose
takeaways: New ARR beat plan by $200k, ending ARR by only $150k
Churned ARR rose from $300k in Q2 to $480k in Q3
slides.source: metrics.csv (ARR movements and plan by quarter).

slides.title: SMB churned ARR more than doubled since Q1 and now offsets a third of new bookings
takeaways: Q3 SMB churn of $390k equals 34% of Q3 new ARR
SMB logo churn rose from 1.8% to 3.1% a month
Mid-market churn is flat at $70-90k a quarter
slides.source: metrics.csv (churned ARR by segment, monthly logo churn). 390 / 1,150 = 34%.

slides.title: If the SMB trend continues, year-end ARR lands about $230k below the $12.0M plan

rows: Rises by the same $170k step as Q2 to Q3

slides.source: metrics.csv; projection uses the assumptions in the right-hand column.

slides.title: Most SMB accounts that churned in Q3 never finished setup in their first 30 days

exhibit.title: SMB accounts that churned in Q3, by setup status, count

takeaways: 44 of 61 churned SMB accounts (72%) never connected their integrations within 30 days
Setup is the common thread among the SMB accounts we lost
slides.source: RevOps pull of the 61 SMB accounts that churned in Q3 (CEO notes). 44 / 61 = 72%.
slides.notes: Finished setup = integrations connected within 30 days of signing.

slides.title: Accounts that finish setup churn at about a fifth of the rate of those that do not

exhibit.title: 90-day churn by setup status, SMB accounts signed Jan-Jun 2026, %

takeaways: Getting accounts through setup is the lever onboarding controls
slides.notes: Cohort analysis; it shows association, which the Q3 churn pull on the previous slide supports.

slides.title: Setup completion fell from 68% to 55% as new accounts per specialist rose 41%
takeaways: The team is still two specialists, as in January
Median days to setup went from 9 to 17
Load per specialist: 42.5 to 60 new accounts a month (+41%)
slides.source: smb_onboarding.csv. Per specialist = new SMB accounts per month / specialists; 60 / 42.5 - 1 = 41%.
slides.notes: Monthly SMB sign-ups rose from 85 to 120 while the team stayed the same.

slides.title: Shifting two Q4 sales hires to onboarding saves $110k a year and recovers about $82k of Q4 ARR

left.heading: Plan as approved: 4 sales hires
bullets: 4 account executives at about $150k each: $600k a year
New hires take about 5 months to ramp, so Q4 bookings barely change

right.heading: Proposed: 2 sales hires + 2 onboarding
bullets: 2 account executives ($300k) and 2 onboarding specialists ($190k): $110k less a year
Two support team members can transfer now
Setting up half of the 170-account backlog saves about $82k of ARR in Q4

slides.source: CEO notes (costs, ramp time, backlog of 170 accounts, average SMB ARR $6.4k). $82k = 85 accounts x (19% - 4%) x $6.4k.
footnotes: The $82k is an estimate: it assumes half the backlog is set up in Q4 and the cohort churn rates hold.
slides.notes: Costs are fully loaded annual figures.

slides.title: The cost is slower sales capacity in 2027, which Sales has not yet sized

left.heading: What we give up
bullets: Two fewer account executives ramping into 2027
Sales has not yet modelled the effect on 2027 new ARR
VP Sales brings that model to the January board

right.heading: What we keep
bullets: Q4 bookings: new hires would add little before they ramp
A fix for the cause of SMB churn before it grows further

slides.source: CEO notes (ramp time, costs); Sales capacity model to follow in January.
slides.notes: Be explicit that the 2027 effect is open and when it will be sized.

slides.title: We ask the board to approve the swap and a revised year-end forecast of $11.85M

items.action: Approve converting two Q4 sales requisitions into onboarding specialists
items.detail: Two support team members transfer now; saves $110k a year

items.action: Accept a revised year-end ARR forecast of $11.85M
items.detail: $11.77M projection plus about $82k recovered by onboarding

items.action: Review SMB churn and the 2027 sales capacity model
items.detail: Setup completion back above 60% is the first test

slides.notes: Two decisions today, one review in January.

slides.title: Cash runway stays near 22 months at the current $650k monthly burn

rows: Effect of the swap on annual cost

footnotes: The swap lowers annual cost slightly; runway is not the constraint.
